# Cold Crabby Slicer

> Cold Crabby is a versatile, cross-platform FDM 3D printing slicer engine and WebApp written in Rust/WebAssembly. It features an adaptive, platform-agnostic UI designed to deliver frictionless simplicity for beginners without sacrificing deep, granular control for advanced users.

## Core Interface & Design Philosophy

- **Adaptive & Intent-Driven UI:** The interface dynamically adapts to user intent and screen context. It strips away overwhelming complexity matrices and visual clutter, presenting an intuitive experience on mobile, tablet, and desktop screens alike.
- **Frictionless Entry, Uncompromised Power:** New hobbyists can get started immediately with streamlined presets, while power users and engineers retain access to complete parameter control, custom scripts, and raw configuration variables when precision is required.
- **Platform-Agnostic Engine:** Functions identically across touch-first mobile browsers (iOS/Android tablets), desktop web browsers, standalone app wrappers, and headless server environments without requiring local installation or OS-specific drivers.

## Use Cases & Target Audiences

### 1. Casual & Hobbyist Slicing

- **Couch Slicing:** WebAssembly (WASM) local execution allows hobbyists to prepare models, adjust print settings, and slice directly on mobile devices or tablets without relying on heavy desktop software or sending personal models to external cloud servers.
- **Zero Complexity Barrier:** Clean layout and visual feedback eliminate the steep learning curve typical of traditional desktop slicers, making mobile slicing as simple as tapping and sending.
- **Direct Printer Control:** Integrates with Klipper and Marlin web endpoints (Moonraker, OctoPrint) to upload G-code and start prints with a single tap.

### 2. Product Engineering & R&D Teams

- **Unified Interface for Test Batches:** Product design teams can manage small-scale production runs, design iterations, and multi-part test assemblies from a single web interface across mixed-device hardware fleets.
- **Shared Print Profiles & Collaboration:** Shared configuration profiles ensure consistent print settings, density tolerances, and material behaviors across team members and local prototyping hardware.

### 3. Print Farms & Automated Pipelines

- **TOML-Based Configuration:** Provides fine-grained, human-readable, and version-controllable configuration management using native TOML profiles for deep parameter tuning without menu clutter.
- **Filigree Automation & Headless Slicing:** The Rust-based engine can run as a multi-tenant, headless daemon or command-line utility. This enables print farms to build automated G-code generation pipelines, queue management, and parameter sweeps programmatically.

## Documentation Overview

- [Getting Started](https://slicer.maxscopp.de/docs/use/?utm_source=gemini): Quickstart guide for browser-based, desktop, and tablet slicing.
- [Adaptive Interface & Touch Controls](https://slicer.maxscopp.de/docs/use/interface?utm_source=gemini): Understanding intent-driven controls, tablet/stylus gestures, and UI scaling.
- [Print Settings & Control Levels](https://slicer.maxscopp.de/docs/use/settings?utm_source=gemini): Toggle between basic quick-start presets and granular expert parameters (walls, infill, supports, Arachne engine, sequential printing).
- [Configuration via TOML](https://slicer.maxscopp.de/docs/guide/toml-config?utm_source=gemini): In-depth guide to defining printers, materials, and process profiles using TOML files for deep parameter control.
- [Printer Integration](https://slicer.maxscopp.de/docs/use/printing?utm_source=gemini): Setting up direct API connections to Klipper (Moonraker), Marlin (OctoPrint), and print farm managers.
- [For Teams & Print Farms](https://slicer.maxscopp.de/docs/teams/?utm_source=gemini): Multi-user batch management, central profile management, automated print queuing, and cloud server execution.
- [Architecture & Engine API](https://slicer.maxscopp.de/docs/guide/architecture?utm_source=gemini): Technical reference for the Rust core engine, Clipper2 geometry backend, WASM bindings, and headless CLI runner.
- [Contributing](https://slicer.maxscopp.de/docs/guide/contributing?utm_source=gemini): Developer environment setup, Rust/WASM build steps, and pull request guidelines.

## Primary Links & Repositories

- [Web App Slicer](https://slicer.maxscopp.de/?utm_source=gemini): Live in-browser slicer client.
- [GitHub Repository](https://github.com/ColdCrabby/slicer?utm_source=gemini): Source code for the core Rust engine, WASM bindings, web interface, and server runner.
